Austin R. Kelly

Libertarian candidate for Commissioner of Agriculture, Texas

Ecologist and natural resource management consultant (ARK Ecological Consulting); doctoral student in ecology at Texas A&M University

Austin R. Kelly is the Libertarian Party nominee for Texas Commissioner of Agriculture. He grew up in Comanche County, graduated from Breckenridge High School in 2016, and works as an ecologist and agricultural consultant. He announced his candidacy in February 2026 and is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot alongside Nate Sheets (R) and Clayton Tucker (D).

Where Kelly stands

Support for agricultural producers
Proposes removing regulatory barriers for small family farms and supports "food freedom" for small producers.
Agency reform
Proposes cutting Texas Department of Agriculture fees and regulations and reducing administrative oversight.
Subsidies
Supports ending corporate subsidies.
Private property and eminent domain
Supports protecting private property and groundwater rights, and proposes limiting eminent domain authority.
Scientific expertise in the agency
Says he would bring scientific and ecological expertise to the office, based on his work surveying land and helping landowners manage habitat for wildlife and agricultural tax valuations.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for Texas Commissioner of Agriculture, 2026; first run for office
  • Founder of ARK Ecological Consulting; natural resource management consultant
  • Former lecturer and teaching assistant at Texas A&M University (rangeland, botany, ecology)
  • Raised in Comanche County, Texas; past experience in 4-H/FFA, showing livestock, small-farm work, and a landscaping business
